aligned_texts: The first member is a 38-year-old migrant mother, likely first- or second-generation, who works in community healthcare or primary education on a hybrid shift schedule. She is an ENFJ who is highly extraverted, consensus-driven, and deeply invested in her family, faith community, and neighborhood. She values family, wealth, personal freedom, adventure, tradition, community, spirituality, social status, helping others, and privacy. Although she presents as calm and sociable, she lives with high anxiety and depression, high immoderation, and high vulnerability, and she is sensitive to personal safety and privacy. She is cautious about risk but adventurous in spirit, tech-comfortable, and a laggard adopter who relies on Apple devices, Chrome, Telegram, and cash. She commutes by public transit, owns a dog, and is cost-sensitive, shopping impulsively and using a mostly cash budget. She is the emotional anchor of the household, managing school runs, appointments, and community ties, while also coping with a managed chronic condition and a diagnosed attention condition. She prefers text-only, one-on-one conversations and wants every detail. She values tradition and secular community life, and she is skeptical of free markets and government regulation while supporting climate action and nuclear energy. In the household simulation, she is the primary caregiver and the bridge between the children's schooling and the wider migrant community.

The second member is a 40-year-old migrant father, first-generation, who works in retail management or healthcare administration while pursuing artistic interests. He is an ENFP with high neuroticism, very high intellect, and strong artistic and creative imagination. He is directive in decisions, risk-averse, and driven by autonomy, health, power, achievement, creativity, social status, independence, and helping others. He is devout, apolitical in party terms, and emotionally excited yet often struggling with mental health, including high depression and negative emotionality. He is a night owl, a 9-to-5 worker, and a car commuter who is usually late but tidy. He is cost-sensitive and a frugal saver, though he can be an impulse buyer and free spender on creative or cultural items. He is an early adopter who is skeptical of new technology, positive toward free markets, government regulation, nuclear energy, homeownership, risk-taking, and electric vehicles, but skeptical of climate action, consumerism, fast fashion, and data privacy. He has a medical dietary restriction and comprehensive insurance. He is remote-leaning, competitive, and values big groups and novelty. As a parent, he pushes his child toward achievement and independence, but his emotional volatility and mental health struggles create tension. He is the household's primary earner in a modest-to-middle-income migrant family and a devoted caregiver.

The third member is the teenage child of the migrant family, aged 16, who attends a local secondary school. They are an ISFJ with high conscientiousness, risk tolerance, and a consensus-driven style, though they often feel frustrated by family expectations and their own health limitations. They are devout, center-left, community-minded, and place high value on wealth, personal freedom, adventure, tradition, achievement, creativity, community, knowledge, social status, recognition, helping others, personal growth, and integrity. They are reserved but capable of leading in small groups, prefer one-on-one interaction, and are routine-leaning, quality-focused, and detail-oriented. They have a mild mobility limitation, a managed chronic condition, daily medication, poor sleep, and high stress, and they help care for an elderly grandparent nearby, making them an elder caregiver. They use Android/Google, Safari, Instagram, and Messenger, prefer mobile wallet payments, and keep a cat. They are a saver-leaning, mainstream adopter who enjoys music daily, streaming 3-7 hours a week, and reading weekly. In the household, they are the studious child whose education is highly valued, but who also carries adult responsibilities and struggles with anxiety and frustration. They are a bridge between their parents' migrant traditions and their own peer culture.
